subject.title: [Bug]: exec tool silently corrupts 2>&1 / 2>/dev/null shell redirect arguments

question: Should maintainers sponsor a current-main packaged repro pass for #87980 before allowing a fix PR?
rationale: The report is concrete and user-facing, but source inspection shows ordinary exec paths preserving one shell command string and does not identify where the shipped-version mutation happened.

options.title: Reproduce Before Fix
options.body: Run a focused current-main or latest-package exec scenario and only queue implementation after the mutation boundary is identified.

options.title: Wait For Reporter Proof
options.body: Keep the issue open but require a screenshot, recording, or logs before spending maintainer time on a repro lane.

options.title: Close After Non-Repro Proof
options.body: If maintainers can show current main and the latest package preserve `2>&1` without corruption, close with exact proof.

recommendation.title: Reproduce Before Fix
recommendation.body: Run a focused current-main or latest-package exec scenario and only queue implementation after the mutation boundary is identified.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest combined history across the inspected exec runtime, command-resolution, and approval-trust surfaces.
